feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it presents a clear leadership narrative, solid platform expertise, and relevant scale indicators. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly repetitive and text-dense, with some structural overlap that reduces impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary establish a focused brand in digital platforms, governance, communications systems, and AI-enabled experiences.  
- Good credibility signals: named employer progression, measurable scope (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and concrete platforms/tools strengthen trust.  
- Strong breadth with relevance: combines strategy, technical execution, analytics, editorial operations, and multimedia in a way that fits senior digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified results (growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost/time savings) would increase impact.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent; punctuation in lists varies; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “10×20-foot” may be safer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add scale or scope from recent roles, e.g., “Led modernization of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace “AI-enabled user experiences” with a more concrete phrase like “AI-enabled search and content discovery” to match the CV evidence.
- Consider a sharper second sentence focused on outcomes: “Builds scalable systems that improve publishing consistency, audience discovery, and cross-channel communications performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities repeats core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be sharper if grouped around distinctive leadership strengths rather than repeating broad phrases already proven elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing for parallel structure: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider replacing “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Change “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer specificity.
- Use “and” instead of “&” for consistency with the rest of the CV’s more formal style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening to 6 items or making it more distinct from those sections.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will make it scan faster and feel more distinct.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a consistent verb-led format and trim filler: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Produced.”
- Make outcomes or purpose clearer in each item, e.g., “to improve policy discovery,” “to support campaign growth,” “to extend conference engagement.”
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and include commas consistently in lists.
- Consider shortening to one line per project and emphasizing the most recent/highest-value examples first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search,” the microsite, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo bullets; reframe these as selected examples or add distinct results/technical scope.
- “Built” appears repeatedly; vary with “Led,” “Developed,” or “Launched” for better rhythm.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around 3–4 priority contributions and add outcomes, scope, or named initiatives where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web modernization for a national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Keep the AI search work, but specify stage or result if possible: “Leading an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available (sites supported, users, launch status, efficiency gains).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “analytics” repeat heavily from the Director role; frame this entry as advisory/consulting impact, not team leadership.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with the biggest enterprise outcomes: website migration, analytics infrastructure, then studio build/governance.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, production cost/time savings, or engagement growth.
- Example rewrite: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers through improved governance and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either quantify distinct gains here or cut it.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries and Recent Projects; emphasize building the in-house studio as the differentiator.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Make it sharper by emphasizing what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletters, video program, editorial coordination, workflow improvement.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter sends/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume, turnaround time improvements.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member outreach.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Improved editorial planning and publishing coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling/operationalizing the program.
- “workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to current scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations” or “Editorial governance” if you want stronger executive/operational emphasis.
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrases only, no mixed formats.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise content strategy for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; avoid repeating exact language.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from exhaustive tools to a sharper headline list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and make it the anchor, since recent roles and projects strongly support it; de-emphasize WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages unless they are important for target roles.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web platforms” or “enterprise CMS modernization” to signal scale rather than listing every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic and leave full platform/tool inventory there.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid expanding it here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the target roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT and could be sharper on business value. Make it more outcome-oriented and less like a raw tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just platform names.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if formatting allows.
- Replace generic phrases with impact language: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and search optimization insights.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & reporting • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool inventory to the technical section.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” or “executive dashboarding.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. It should emphasize higher-level production capability and operational scope rather than basic task labels.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools/tasks to capability-based phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- If space allows, add scale or context tied to recent work: “Broadcast-quality in-house studio production” or “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy and member programming”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “End-to-end video production” or “Studio-based video production”
- Keep only 4 concise bullets; avoid listing entry-level terms unless they differentiate you

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use more specific wording here to avoid repetition
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet about building an in-house studio, so this skills item should complement, not restate, that achievement

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior profile, this item should signal depth and relevance, especially Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest, most recent platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint / Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/context rather than just names: e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration), WordPress, SharePoint/Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and better alignment with the rest of the CV.
- If no context can be added, keep only the most relevant tools and drop lower-signal items to avoid a filler feel.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed version in one place only.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience, so avoid repeating it across multiple skills sections without added specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation** to signal applied capability.
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in brief: **Front-end implementation, tag deployment, serverless scripting and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless required by the role; they add little value at this level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- If you keep this item, reduce overlap in Topline Skills or use this section for tools not named elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item mixes true automation platforms with general collaboration/project tools, which weakens the “systems” signal. Since workflow automation is already a core competency, this line should emphasize build/use depth and reduce generic overlap.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two clearer categories or rename for precision: “Automation & Workflow Platforms” rather than “Automation & Workflow Systems.”
- Prioritize actual automation/database tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier”; move Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello to a separate “Project & Collaboration Tools” line if space allows.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Airtable databases and workflow systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams.”
- If accurate, add level/context elsewhere, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate,” since tool names alone don’t show impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams read as generic workplace tools unless tied to workflow/process use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise email/CRM capability and aligning the wording with the scale described in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite content as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter and campaign delivery**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show depth: **audience segmentation**, **journey automation**, or **member communications**
- Keep the list concise; prioritize the most recent/strategic platform first, which you already do with Dynamics 365

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already covered there.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless clarified as email/CRM/member engagement.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” It should either be tightened to emphasize execution-level capabilities or removed if space is tight.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to show capability, not just tools: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing”
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a stronger outcome-oriented term like “KPI reporting” or “performance reporting.”
- Consider ordering by strategic weight and recency: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity, then SEO/experimentation.
- If you have proof points elsewhere, align wording to recent impact: e.g., “analytics infrastructure,” “leadership reporting,” or “performance analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly a repeat of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one version more strategic and this one more tool-specific.
- “A/B testing” may overstate experience unless supported in recent roles; use “experimentation” if broader and safer.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available output metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video updates, size/timing of website refresh, or channels supported.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a fuller version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and standardize multi-channel publishing workflows across web, email, social, and video.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more executional than strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project outputs, while trimming generic support language.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around the most distinctive contribution: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county-facing programs and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more active, specific phrase such as “produced supporting digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; 1 sentence or 2 concise bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with the 2015–2024 NACo roles; avoid repeating broad digital/media language already covered more strongly later.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is vague and may duplicate advocacy/editorial coordination themes from later entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize software/tool fluency, not production capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
